title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.20597v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead. We propose \name, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets. translated_title: 面向语言智能体的行动与预测协同演化
translated_abstract: 训练语言智能体的瓶颈在于长程轨迹 rollout 的高昂成本，而标准的智能体强化学习（RL）仅从最终标量奖励中学习，导致中间步骤的监督信号在很大程度上未被利用。先前的工作通过两类方式利用这种监督：一是估计每步成功概率的价值目标，二是拟合环境响应的观测目标。但两者都难以良好构造：(1) 价值目标来自轨迹中每个步骤同一的单一标量信号；(2) 观测目标（如网页和终端日志）冗长且含噪，且只能向前预测一步。我们提出 \name，引入第三种监督目标——多步动作目标。在成功的同策略轨迹上，\name 训练策略主干生成每个历史之后所跟随的动作序列。当从先前历史进行预测时，每个动作也会受到监督，从而形成一个时间集成，……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出在成功的同策略轨迹上引入多步动作序列作为监督目标，使行动生成与动作预测协同演化，从而充分利用中间步骤的监督信号，缓解语言智能体训练中长程 rollout 成本高、终端奖励稀疏的问题。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes co-evolving acting and forecasting by adding multi-step action targets on successful on-policy trajectories, enabling language agents to exploit intermediate-step supervision beyond sparse terminal rewards and reduce the cost of long-horizon rollouts.
